To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 1. 7 kb TP2 transcript is created by splicing across the terminal repeats and is transcribed from the TP2 latent promoter, located in a bidirectional latent transcription unit with the TP1 promoter.
the TP2 transcript is spliced to a different 5′ exon and that the 3.3-kb TP2 promoter is bidirectional with the TP1 promoter.

the terminal protein gene 1 (TP1) and the terminal protein gene2 (TP2) of Epstein Barr virus (EBV), are expressed from a bidirectional promoter region and that the 1.8 kb TP1 transcript is spliced across the EBV terminal repeats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular biology of the EBV terminal repeat and the TP genes.
the molecular biology of the terminal protein genes of EBV.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate EBV gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the terminal protein genes 1 and 2 are created by circularization of EBV DNA, and that their mRNAs are expressed from a common promoter region, which is also the origin of transcription of the latent membrane protein gene.
EBV has a bidirectional promoter region, which is responsible for the transcription of the TP2 and LMP RNAs in opposite direction.
TP1 and TP 2 are expressed from different promoters but share a common set of exons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EBV genome is transcribed from at least 10 different promoters, each of which can produce several distinct transcripts.
EBV has a bidirectional promoter region that can transcribe in either direction.
the 1.5 kb and the 1.8 kb RNAs are expressed from the same promoter region, but in different directions, and that the 1 kb RNA is expressed from a separate promoter region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TP2 transcript is expressed from the bidirectional promoter region and is spliced in the same way as TP1 RNA.
the TP2 gene is a novel member of the EBV latent gene family and is expressed in latently infected B cells.
the TP2 transcript is expressed from the same promoter as the LMP1 transcript.
